item.title: America Has Lost Its Leverage Over China
item.description: The Trump-Xi summit will reinforce a new set of implicit rules and assumptions for managing relations that ultimately favor China, argues Henrietta Levin in Foreign Affairs.

item.title: How Might the Trump-Xi Summit Impact U.S. Farmers?
item.description: The U.S. agricultural industry has borne the brunt of the recent U.S.-China trade conflict. Now, farmers watch closely as Presidents Trump and Xi seek a potential agreement in Beijing, but longer-term structural trends make a quick fix unlikely.

item.title: States Weekly: May 13, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers May 13, 2026.

item.title: The AI Escalation Danger Trump and Xi Must Address
item.description: As Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet in Beijing on May 14–15 to discuss the future of U.S.-China AI cooperation, concerns are growing over escalatory tendencies in models like DeepSeek. Common AI benchmarking may offer a path toward safer development.

item.title: A Confident Beijing Welcomes President Trump
item.description: Scott Kennedy lays out how China’s leaders are approaching the upcoming Trump-Xi summit, and why China feels remarkably more confident compared to the first such summit in 2017.

item.title: The U.S.-China Trade Truce Has Not Solved the Gallium Problem
item.description: The upcoming Trump-Xi summit offers an opportunity to press Beijing on its commitments on critical minerals.

item.title: The Deal of the ART: Assessing the “America First” Trade Policy in Asia
item.description: Countries in Asia, especially Southeast Asia, have a lot riding on how U.S.-China trade issues are ultimately resolved.
